Definition: feminine of a derivative of G4291; a patroness, i.e. assistant:--succourer.
BiblicalUsage: Prostatis means a patroness, a helper, one who stands before others for their good. It appears once, of Phoebe: receive her in the Lord, as becometh saints, and assist her in whatsoever business she hath need of you, for she hath been a succourer of many, and of myself also.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Phoebe shows me that the church runs on succourers: one woman's help carried Paul himself, and he never forgot it.
